windowOuter.note: All figures are window.outerWidth/outerHeight (Tauri LogicalSize units, per CLAUDE.md's Logical-only rule) -- these are DPI-independent by design, which is why 100pct and 125pct numbers agree to within 1px rounding. devicePixelRatio was the only value that differed (1.0 vs 1.25), confirming correct per-monitor DPI handling.
windowOuter.fullWindowNote: Switching displayMode to 'full' always opens/centers the window on the PRIMARY monitor (DISPLAY5, 100% scale) regardless of which monitor the pill was on -- this is the app's own designed behavior, not a scripting artifact. A '125%-scale Full window' screenshot was therefore not obtainable without changing the primary monitor's own OS scale, which was out of scope/skipped per the risk rule below. The 100pct_full_*.png set is the only Full-window pixel corpus.

geometryDetail.conclusion: Every logical-px geometry number is identical (or within 1px rounding) between 100% and 125% OS display scale. This confirms the app's Tauri LogicalSize/LogicalPosition discipline (per repo CLAUDE.md hard rule) is holding correctly across DPI -- no DPI-driven layout bugs were found.

knownIssue_scriptedWindowMove: When the pill window was relocated across monitors via raw Win32 SetWindowPos (bypassing Tauri's own drag/move APIs) and then interacted with too soon (<1s), the app's cached window-position/monitor state lagged the real OS position, producing wildly wrong compact-panel offsets (rendered fully off-viewport, blank screenshot). Waiting ~4s after each forced move before the next interaction reliably fixed this every time it was tried. This is a scripting-environment artifact of driving the window via raw OS calls, not a defect verified to reproduce under the app's own drag-to-corner/monitor-follow code paths -- noted for whoever automates this again, not filed as a product bug.
